newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares shed 2.78pct but hold 1,500 level.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares shed 2.78pct but hold 1,500 level.

text.p: Prices of Greek shares tumbled 2.78 percent on Friday to 1,500 points and fund managers said the selling pressure was intentionally directed at blue chips, pushing the broader market lower.

"Selling pressure looks intended to affect the broader market and the benchmark index, because sell orders are placed with no hesitation onto bid prices of blue chips," said Michael Eleftheriou, fund manager at Alpha mutual funds.
Other market participants said they suspected short-selling in OTE. OTE has the largest weight in the bourse's general index.

"Trading behaviour in OTE telecom would only be reasoned if short-selling was allowed in the Greek equity market, but it is not." said a broker. "Big players unload stock which will be in their possession on Monday."
A total of 53.4 million shares of OTE were part-floated in the previous week, with foreign institutional investors snapping up nearly half of the stock.
Fund managers said the market remained resilient, comfortably cushioning the pressure as prices in a wide range of stocks have reached very attractive levels.

"The market features considerable absorption and resilience in the face of such aggressive moves which in previous years, with a less mature market, would have sent prices to a cascade," said Alpha's Eleftheriou.
The drop in prices makes several stocks appear very attractively priced and selective buying is warranted, he added.
Investors were keeping a wary eye on macroeconomic issues but the market fall could not be attributed to this factor solely.

"The macroeconomic outlook has not changed to either direction and the rigidity in consumer price inflation and deteriorating current account figures were already incorporated into prices," Eleftheriou said.

On Thursday, provisional Bank of Greece figures for February 1997 showed a widening in Greece's trade balance and current account deficit, coupled with a drop in May forex reserves to $16.3 billion after a brief attack on the drachma.
On the same day, professor Yiannis Spraos, economic advisor to the prime minister Costas Simitis, submitted a report on economic policy to be pursued in coming years.
Spraos' report called for tough fiscal and incomes policy measures including a one-off 10 percent tax on corporate profits in 1998.
But National Economy Minister Yiannos Papandoniou made clear the government was not considering adopting such a measure.

"The picture given to the market by the Spraos proposals and the government denouncing them is not good because it dented market sentiment and undermined the market's confidence in the government," Eleftheriou said.
The Athens general index ended 2.78 percent or 42.88 points lower at 1,500.37 from Thursday's close of 1,543.25, but slid as low as 1,492.96 in late trades before topping 1,500 points again.
Banks and industrials were particularly battered, giving up 3.48 and 3.19 percent respectively, while other sectors fared better.
Turnover amounted to 20.5 billion drachmas on volume of 5.0 million shares.
